newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: No turning back on NATO expansion - Czech minister.
newsitem.headline: No turning back on NATO expansion - Czech minister.

text.p: Czech Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec said on Thursday he saw no turning back on the enlargement of NATO and that he hoped the U.S.-Russia summit would help build trust on both sides.

Asked whether NATO enlargement would go ahead despite Russian opposition, Zieleniec told Reuters, "I am confident about that. There is no turning back actually and this will be also an important step as regards the stabilisation of the security situation in Europe."

Eastward expansion of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) is the key agenda item for this week's Helsinki summit between Presidents Bill Clinton and Boris Yeltsin. The Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary are seen as the leading candidates to be invited to join after an alliance summit in Madrid in July.

"I hope it (the Helsinki summit) will mean progress as regards building a certain foundation for security dialogue between Russia and the West. Moreover it will mean progress as regards building of relative trust or of improving the atmosphere of trust between the two sides so as to improve the atmosphere before the Madrid summit," Zieleniec said.
However, he cautioned both Russia and the West against struggling for power and influence in Central Europe.

"It is important to clearly state and to make it clear that the central European space is not a space in which Russia and the West should contest for power and influence. Such an idea is quite unacceptable for us," Zieleniec said.
